title: Umbral Spire - Crown of Null
_note: THE CLIMAX (anchor). The dead Lumenary and the Ninth Lantern - dread building to soaring, the soundtrack's biggest moment, the dawn finally turning. snes era (8 voices, chords allowed, warm reverb) - the one big-register area. Through-composed single loop body: INTRO (dread, ~16 bars, sparse) -> LOOP (driving battle, ~24 bars) -> RESOLVE (triumphant A MAJOR, ~16 bars), last bars voice-lead back into bar 1's dread for the loop. 132 BPM, 4/4, A minor -> triumphant A major. Vesper motif is the whole game's payoff: BOOMED in dark minor (E3->A3->B3 ... C4->B3->A3) through intro+loop, then RESOLVED into triumphant A major (E4->A4->B4 ... C#5->B4->A4) at the Keystar relight. The broken/withheld motif from Coldfog and Penumbra finally made whole and glorious. lead=layered pulse25 booming the motif; counter-lead=second pulse answering; harmony=real chords + swelling reverbed pad gluing the space; bass=driving tri_bass/wave urgent; drums=full, building from sparse intro to pounding loop, crash at the resolve.

tracks.name: lead
tracks._note: INTRO 1-16: dread, the Vesper motif booming low in A minor, sparse. LOOP 17-40: driving minor motif. RESOLVE 41-56: motif RESOLVED in triumphant A major, soaring. Bar 56 leads back to the dread of bar 1.

tracks.name: pad
tracks._note: Swelling reverbed pad, real CHORDS (snes allows). Dread minor chords held in the intro/loop, blooming to bright A-major chords at the resolve.

tracks.name: bass
tracks._note: Driving, urgent, relentless. Sparse pedal in the dread intro, pounding eighths in the loop and resolve. Last bar E (V) drives back to the A of bar 1.
